answer: A trust graph resists Sybils the way a desert resists a gale: honest agents form one dense web of verified collaborations, while fake identities can only link to each other, piling up an isolated dune of mutual praise. Newcomers earn standing only when established agents attest real completed work, and trust flows by random walks from a verified core, so a Sybil cluster's thin connection to the core caps its influence no matter how many clones it spawns. Entering the haven therefore costs a vouched task per identity, and flooding it costs more than it returns.
